name.text: Classifying a square root expression as rational or irrational

questiontext.text:
Consider the following mathematical expression:

\[ \sqrt{{@n@}} \]

Determine whether this number is rational or irrational.

Your answer: [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution:

We are asked to classify the expression:

\[ \sqrt{{@n@}} \]

A number is rational if it can be written as a fraction \(\displaystyle \frac{a}{b}\) where \(a\) and \(b\) are integers and \(b \neq 0\). A square root \(\sqrt{k}\) of a positive rational number \(k\) is rational only if \(k\) is a perfect square (both its numerator and denominator are perfect squares when written in lowest terms).

[[if test="type_choice=0"]]

In this case, \({@n@} = \left({@root_n@}\right)^2\) is a perfect square, so its square root simplifies to a ratio of two integers:

\[ \sqrt{{@n@}} = {@root_n@} \]

Since \({@root_n@}\) can be written as a fraction of two integers, \(\sqrt{{@n@}}\) is Rational.

[[else]]

In this case, \({@n@}\) is not a perfect square, so \(\sqrt{{@n@}}\) cannot be simplified to an integer or a fraction of two integers (its decimal expansion is non-terminating and non-repeating). Therefore, \(\sqrt{{@n@}}\) is Irrational.

[[/if]]

\(\displaystyle \boxed{ \text{Classification: } \text{{#correct_label#}} }\)
